💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, you’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG.
  • This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.
  • Sources indicate that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, you’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Sources indicate that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

In a recent development, coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios claims the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

Recent findings suggest that the game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

As it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Industry observers note that though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

Audi Patents Physical Buttons That Fold Out from Behind a Touchscreen

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (324 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Physical buttons have a lot going for them.
  • As CarMoses first discovered, Audi has filed a patent application that describes a motorized switch bar, which pivots out from behind the display’s lower edge.
  • For those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Physical buttons have a lot going for them. They’re easy to find by feel, satisfying to use, and generally pretty good at staying wherever the automaker installed them. Well, it seems Audi has an idea that would change that last part. It involves hiding the buttons behind a touchscreen and deploying them when needed.

As CarMoses first discovered, Audi has filed a patent application that describes a motorized switch bar, which pivots out from behind the display’s lower edge. The screen stays fixed, while the physical controls swing into position beneath it. Interestingly, when stowed, the bar apparently has an on-screen counterpart with the same functions lined up in the same order, so those who don’t want physical buttons can avoid them entirely.

See all results for used Audi for sale near 63042.

For those who do want the physical buttons, there are plenty of reasons to get excited. First, Audi says in its patent documents with the German government that the switches can deploy at startup, via voice controls, or via gestures. Moving the controls from the screen to the physical switches also provides more total screen room for users. (In one example, the physical bar deploys when a movie opens, leaving more room for the video.).

Industry observers note that ultimately, this could be a great way to meet the demands of more people. Designers love a clean dashboard without physical buttons and switches, but plenty of drivers really love having that switchgear. This system allows owners to pick whatever they want on the fly.

The timing makes plenty of sense too. Audi has openly said that it views moving toward more mechanical controls as the right direction. Of course, adding extra complexity to the once-simple idea of buttons can also increase the cost down the line when it comes time for repairs, but even so, this idea is certainly a fascinating solution to a very modern problem.

Tested: 2027 Audi SQ7 Is the Punchier 3-Row SUV

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1454 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Audi is slicing its bread thin when it comes to three-row performance SUVs.
  • According to recent reports, our expert editors test every vehicle we review.
  • Every SQ7 comes with Audi’s familiar 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 under the hood, and this version makes 90 hp more than the outgoing model.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Audi is slicing its bread thin when it comes to three-row performance SUVs. Below the flagship SQ9, there’s now a 2027 Audi SQ7. It’s the SQ9’s doppelgänger, minus a few inches of length and wearing what will be a more familiar badge for longtime Audi buyers. This is the third generation of Q7 and, like before, it straddles the space between a BMW X5 and X7, or a Mercedes-Benz GLE and GLS. And thankfully, the S model marches on with a bruiser of a V-8 engine. Audi pitched it as the SUV for the “performance family,” which is a concept that may have lost a little in translation. No matter the 0–60 of your family, though, this SQ7 is more than adept at moving lots of people around in a fast, fun manner.

According to recent reports, our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

Every SQ7 comes with Audi’s familiar 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 under the hood, and this version makes 90 hp more than the outgoing model. The numbers come in at 590 hp and 591 lb-ft of torque, sent through the same fresh, rear-biased Quattro all-whee- drive system that debuted on the SQ9. Shifting is handled by a ZF eight-speed automatic transmission, and Audi claims a 3.7-second 0–60-mph time, one-tenth quicker than the bigger SQ9. When equipped with optional summer rubber, the SQ7 tops out at a limited 155 mph.

Transmission: Eight-speed automatic, all-wheel drive.

EPA MPG: 15/20/17 mpg (city/highway/combined).

The TL;DR summary? Refer to my Audi SQ9 review from last month. The dynamic experience of both cars is overwhelmingly similar. But there are some small but significant differences which are worth exploring in more depth.

In a recent development, like the SQ9, the SQ7 offers an optional Sport adaptive air suspension that lowers the ride height by 0.6 inch, fits more aggressive anti-roll bars, and tweaks the tune of the adaptive dampers and air suspension. While the SQ9 I drove was not fitted with this suspension, the SQ7 I tested was.

According to recent reports, as advertised, this optional suspension is indeed more dynamic than the standard setup. The big SUV went from, sure, you can drive it hard if you want, to, this thing is actually kind of fun. Of course, the 5.5-inch shorter wheelbase, a near-nine-inch reduction in overall length, and the 100-pound diet compared to the SQ9 does some heavy lifting here too. On the Sport setup, the SQ7 turned in more promptly and benefited from notably improved body control. Plus, power distribution is clearly more pronounced from the back axle than it is in the standard Q7 on account of the heavily rear-biased Quattro system shared with the SQ9. It’s still not as rigid or as hardcore as an X7 M60 or an AMG GLE 63 S, but Audi is moving in that direction with its sportier tune.

It has been revealed that the SQ7 makes its V-8 soundtrack known to a slightly more obvious degree than the SQ9 too. This could be down to my slightly closer proximity to the quad-tipped exhaust from the driver’s seat, or minor improvements in sound deadening, but whatever the reason, it’s improved. The V-8 rumble and meaty rip to its 7000-rpm redline were like a luxurious dessert I never tired of taking bites out of. The newly introduced SQ7’s raw pace is improved over the outgoing model, with the extra 90 horses over the previous SQ7 obvious whenever I pushed.

Fuel economy is the major loser here. I looked down after 100 miles of California canyon road driving and noticed the trip computer readout stating 11.4 mpg. More typical driving will be better at 17 mpg combined, per the EPA rating, but expect this big SUV to gulp down the premium stuff.

Sources indicate that there’s little to no penalty in ride when you spec the firmer suspension. The difference is so minute that it took some deep concentration over similar stretches of road to discern any penalty to comfort versus the regular Q7. If anything, there’s a touch of additional flintiness to the biggest impacts, which could just as easily be the fault of the 23-inch wheels and summer tires fitted to the SQ7 compared to the 22-inch all-seasons on the Q7. Whatever the reduction in comfort may be, the drop in ride height is worth it purely from an appearance perspective. With the Midnight Green Metallic–painted body (I know, it looks black) hugging the black-painted multi-spoke wheels, the SQ7 would make for a perfect villain car in a spy thriller.

Industry observers note that here’s where you really need to make the tough decision between SQ7 and SQ9. Are you planning on using the third row frequently? If so, don’t pass go, head directly to the 9. If you’re just in the game for a larger SUV and might use the third row on occasion, then the SQ7 is the one to get. The substantial difference isn’t necessarily in the amount of space for third-row passengers, but in cargo room with the third row in place.

It has been revealed that surprisingly, legroom in the wayback is identical between the two. But clambering into noted space was much tougher in the SQ7 thanks to a narrower crawl-through gap behind the second row (available with a standard bench or optional captain’s chairs). Once situated, life is pretty much the same in both three-row Audis. The 4.2 cubic feet of reduced cargo space in the SQ7 will make it so that you won’t be able to bring as many goodies to the picnic as an SQ9 can carry, though.

Sources indicate that from a driver’s perspective, the SQ7’s cabin is about as good as it gets in a modern Audi. The whole layout, from the screens to the center console and feature set, is identical to the SQ9 flagship, so you could consider this a junior flagship. Optional auto-opening and -closing doors can be had. The Digital Matrix LED headlights that are so astoundingly cool in the SQ9 come standard here. Bang & Olufsen 4-D sound (also optional) with exciters in the seats makes for one hell of an audio experience.

Industry observers note that and if you like screens, Audi’s got ’em. The 11.9-inch digital cluster blends into the 14.5-inch central infotainment system, and the 12.3-inch passenger display comes standard. I wish there were more physical controls, especially for the frustrating screen-controlled air vents, but at least Audi supplies some buttons and knobs both on the steering wheel and center console.

Luxury accoutrements by way of unexpected or interesting material usage are plentiful. The carbon-weave trim stands out versus traditional glossy carbon fiber. Funky fabrics on the doors and contrast stitching are appropriately nice touches. Audi claims it’s trying to do better with how it presents its interiors by doing away with piano-black plastic, and while this effort is a good start, there’s still plenty to go around on the dash, steering wheel, and center console.

The approximately $19,000 you’ll save on the SQ7 over the SQ9 sure is a motivating factor for picking the smaller three-row. Its slightly better driving dynamics are another good one, but again, it’s all about priorities here. An extra-large family would be better served by the larger option.

It has been revealed that for now, BMW doesn’t offer an X5 M60 with a V-8, and the AMG price match is the inline-six PHEV GLE 53. In other words, this gas-powered V-8 performance SUV has a little niche of its own for the time being. A Porsche Cayenne S is considerably more expensive to start, and the gap only widens when the option book comes into play.

According to recent reports, there’s a lot going for this latest generation of Audi’s smaller three-row, and outside of some small digital quirks you need to get over, it talks a persuasive game. Audi nailed the powertrain with this V-8 and its rear-biased Quattro system. And despite the SQ7’s sporty potential, there’s little compromise when it comes to usability here. The styling is arguably a bit soft in spots, but it has far more attitude than the brand’s electric offerings thanks to an upright face and pronounced fender flares.

The rear-wheel steering does an excellent job of making the SQ7 drive smaller than it should. It comes standard and can turn the rear wheels up to five degrees in the opposite direction to tighten the turning radius or make the SUV dive into corners with the eagerness you’d expect from a much smaller vehicle. This, combined with lighter-than-typical and progressive steering from Audi, removed that sensation of excessive size from the driver’s seat.

The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Toyota is about to unveil its first extended-range EV, and it looks like the Highlander

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV.
  • The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).
  • Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV.

The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).

Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.

Sources indicate that EREVs use a smaller battery than a pure electric vehicle, while the engine is typically smaller than a PHEV. While they are quieter and often cheaper than a plug-in, EREVs are also less efficient than a pure EV.

A Nikkei report in September claimed that Toyota was preparing to begin production of its first EREV in China in Spring 2027.

It appears the rumors are true. Toyota’s joint venture in China, GAC Toyota, posted a preview on its Weibo account with the caption #Toyota doesn’t rush but range-extended.

Toyota didn’t confirm the name, but all signs point to it being the Highlander EREV. The blurry preview looks like the Highlander, and when translated into English, a part of the text below it reads “Cash in on the classics. Global flagship SUV. Not a quick fix, but a range extender.”.

GAC Toyota will reveal the fresh EREV at the Guangzhou Motor Show on November 27. Check back for the full details.

According to the Nikkei report, Toyota aims to produce 200,000 EREVs in 2027. In 2028, it expects production to double to around 400,000 units.

While Toyota likely won’t bring the extended-range EV to the US, it is set to launch the fully electric version of its three-row Highlander in early 2027 (shown above on the left).

The all-electric Toyota Highlander BEV will be available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrains with two battery packs: 77 kWh or 95.8 kWh. The smaller (77 kWh) battery provides up to 287 miles of range, while the larger (95.8 kWh) battery provides up to 320 miles in FWD models.

Inside, the electric Toyota Highlander EV offers three rows of seating with room for up to seven passengers.

The three-row electric SUV will be built at Toyota’s manufacturing plant in Georgetown, Kentucky.

Like most foreign brands, Toyota is struggling to keep up with domestic brands like BYD, Geely, and Chery in China’s brutal auto market.

However, it’s Toyota’s gas and hybrid cars that are getting crushed by the competition. In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, about 19% fewer than in the same period last year.

After sales plunged nearly 20%, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower year-over-year sales, Toyota noted the market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected.”.

Meanwhile, BYD introduces a self-driving SUV with 600 miles of range that recharges in 10 minutes. These guys are toast.

Toyota looks to avoid the intensifying price war with pure electric vehicles in China. An EREV can potentially be offered at a premium, especially as a flagship SUV.

A organization executive mentioned (via Nikkei) that “Competition in China is intensifying as the market fixates on battery EVs, leading to price wars among automakers,” adding, “We need to take steps to avoid being dragged into that competition.”.

Will an EREV help power Toyota’s comeback in China? Or is it late to the party once again? Share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Volkswagen is moving back to more physical buttons, after suffering some backlash from its touch-button-heavy design. Mercedes also publicly recognized that maybe the world went too far with touchscreens. Audi, too, seems to be eyeing more physical controls. But it isn't giving up its touchscreen ones to do so. The organization just patented a technology that lets it have its cake and eat it, too, but creating a physical button panel that can hide behind a touchscreen.

It has been revealed that unearthed by CarMoses, this patent reveals off a little button bar, which is just a strip of physical buttons and possibly one knob that lives below the touchscreen. At the press of a button, or even with voice control, the button bar can hide away behind the touchscreen, for anyone who prefers a simpler looking cabin. Once the buttons are hidden, the touchscreen creates a duplicate set of icons at the bottom, so button functionality isn't lost while hidden.

What sort of physical buttons will occupy such a button bar? There seems to be a circular knob in the center of the buttons, so that will likely be volume. The flanking buttons could be for climate control, maybe heated seats, or perhaps even some drive mode buttons. Whatever they end up being, it will be nice to see Audi's with high-quality physical buttons again.

Sources indicate that in the '90s, 2000s, and 2010s, Audi had some of the best buttons, switches, and knobs in the industry, all with satisfying, high-quality clicks. The current crop of piano-black plastic touch buttons in most modern Audis feels like a slap in the face for fans of the brand. So to see the return of some buttons in places where they can be easily memorized and adjusted without looking would be wonderful.

Recent findings suggest that obviously, Audi can't use physical buttons for everything. There are far too many controls and features in modern cars for that to work. There'd be hundreds of buttons on the dashboard if that were the case. But the main buttons, the ones you use everyday, should be physical. And the beauty of this patent is that it, if you like a more high-tech vibe, you can hide them away. With this patent, Audi gets to make both camps happy.

Breaking: Best Cars for Snow

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When discussing a car’s performance in the snow, it all comes down to tires and clearance.
  • According to recent reports, so, when selecting this list of best vehicles for snow, we included only top-rated models that come standard from the factory with tires rated for severe snow service.
  • In a recent development, it’s also important to mention that any car with winter tires would be our preferred method of transportation in snowy conditions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When discussing a car’s performance in the snow, it all comes down to tires and clearance. Tires are the only part of your vehicle that makes contact with the road, so the rubber mounted on your car is the number-one determiner of how much grip you’ll have while accelerating, turning, or braking on slippery surfaces such as snow and ice. All-wheel drive may help you get going in the snow, but it doesn’t help you stop.

According to recent reports, so, when selecting this list of best vehicles for snow, we included only top-rated models that come standard from the factory with tires rated for severe snow service. These tires are marked with the all-important three-peak mountain snowflake icon (3PMSF). This icon is found on either all-weather tires or all-terrain tires that have been tested and are capable of at least 110 percent of the traction of a reference all-season tire. Not every all-terrain tire carries this marking.

In a recent development, it’s also important to mention that any car with winter tires would be our preferred method of transportation in snowy conditions. If you don’t want to pony up for one of these SUVs or trucks with their often pricey optional off-road packages that include the 3PMSF tires, consider outfitting a different vehicle with winter tires. Check out our Winter Tire Buying Guide for advice on which tires to choose.

The CX-50 is one of our favorite compact SUVs, and it offers a rugged-looking trim level called the Meridian Edition. This version comes with snow-rated all-terrain tires no matter whether you choose the naturally aspirated 2.5 S Meridian Edition or the more powerful Turbo Meridian Edition.

Tire: General Grabber A/T or Pirelli Scorpion XTM A/T.

In a recent development, if you’re not willing to go all out for the Raptor version of the F-150 found later on this list, this popular pickup truck also offers a lesser off-road trim level that also comes with snow-rated tires. The F-150 Tremor doesn’t have the upgraded engine or suspension from the Raptor, but it does have style upgrades and other modifications compared with the standard F-150. There are two factory tire choices, either General or Pirelli, but both have the 3PMSF icon.

It has been revealed that many versions of the Ram 1500 pickup offer an Off-Road Group option package that includes Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires in various sizes, all of which have the 3PMSF icon. Ironically enough, the Ram’s most off-road-oriented versions—the Rebel, RHO, and TRX—also have all-terrain tires, but not ones specifically rated for snow.

The GX is closely related to the Toyota Land Cruiser and is the most off-road-ready SUV in the Lexus lineup. To get snow-rated tires from the factory, you have to opt for the Overtrail model, which comes with all-terrain tires and other upgrades meant to improve the GX’s performance in the dirt and other types of off-road terrain. It has an impressive 9.8 inches of ground clearance.

Ford Ranger Raptor, Ford F-150 Raptor, Ford Bronco Raptor.

Tire: BFGoodrich All-Terrain T/A K02 and K03.

Recent findings suggest that the BFGoodrich K0 series of off-road tires is well regarded among off-road enthusiasts. Ford’s Raptor off-road pickups, the Ranger and F-150, come with the latest K03 tires, while the Bronco Raptor SUV comes with K02s. We’re fans of all of these high-performance 4x4s, but the Ranger Raptor is our favorite of the bunch due to its smaller size, lower base price, and subdued styling.

In a recent development, subaru has offered standard all-wheel drive on nearly all of its models for quite a while now, which has earned it a reputation for all-weather performance. But not every Subaru comes with tires optimized for snow. Only the Wilderness version of the Outback mid-size SUV comes with Yokohama Geolandar All-Terrain tires that carry this rating. (The Forester Wilderness and Crosstrek Wilderness also have these tires, but those models don’t rate as high in our testing.).

Mercedes-Benz G550 with G Professional Package.

Sources indicate that no, you probably don’t need a G-wagen to traipse through a few inches of snow to get to the grocery store. But this highly capable SUV has become a style icon for its distinctive aesthetic, and for good reason. The most capable version of the G-class is the G550 with the G Professional package, which adds all-terrain tires, a roof rack, a bull bar on the front, and other off-road upgrades.

Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail and Rally.

The Mustang Mach-E compact electric SUV is one of the few vehicles you can get from the factory with all-weather tires, in this case the Michelin CrossClimate2. These snow-rated tires come on certain versions of the Mach-E, including the high-performance, 480-hp Rally and the latest-for-2027 Trail (pictured), which also has extra ground clearance.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ford’s return to the top class of the 24 Hours of Le Mans was finally unveiled during the Thanksgiving Day NFL game between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, along with an official name that clearly evokes the firm’s past success: GT41.
  • Industry observers note that of course, there weren’t 39 cars before the GT40, as that name comes from the fact that the car was 40 inches tall.
  • Sources indicate that and while the GT41 is based off the same Oreca chassis as used by the Genesis GMR-001 and outgoing Alpine A424 and Acura ARX-06, the car and team is a wholly internal Ford effort.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ford’s return to the top class of the 24 Hours of Le Mans was finally unveiled during the Thanksgiving Day NFL game between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, along with an official name that clearly evokes the firm’s past success: GT41.

Industry observers note that of course, there weren’t 39 cars before the GT40, as that name comes from the fact that the car was 40 inches tall. The GT41, for what it’s worth is 41 inches tall… almost. Technically, the car is 41.7 inches from the ground to the top of its air intake, a dimension dictated by the current FIA regulations for the LMDh class. But GT42 doesn’t quite have the same ring to it.

Sources indicate that and while the GT41 is based off the same Oreca chassis as used by the Genesis GMR-001 and outgoing Alpine A424 and Acura ARX-06, the car and team is a wholly internal Ford effort. “Everything that we’re building, it’s in-house,” said Mark Rushbrook, global director of Ford Racing, “It's the design, the engineering, the development, all the technical elements of the car.”.

According to recent reports, that internal approach particularly applies to the engine, which Rushbrook calls the heart of the car. The naturally aspirated 5.4-liter V-8 is based off Ford’s production engines, so much so that the block is shared with the supercharged 5.2-liter in the Mustang Dark Horse SC and F-150 Raptor R and is pulled straight from the line at the Essex Engine Plant in Windsor, Ontario. Assembled inside Ford’s dyno lab at the tech giant’s headquarters in Dearborn, Michigan, every part inside the racing engine “is designed by a Ford engineer,” according to Joseph Hendrickson, motorsports powertrain calibration engineer. “The engines are also tested on a dynamometer inside the same building. It’s a huge point of pride for us,” he said.

The final livery of the GT41 that will race at Le Mans will be revealed closer to the start of the 2027 WEC calendar, which being at Qatar in March. The car seen here features a camouflage pattern made of the Ford Racing wordmark, with Easter eggs hidden throughout that reflect the team’s pride as an American and Detroit-based automaker; look closely, and you’ll see an American flag, a bald eagle head, the Statue of Liberty, the Spirit of Detroit, and a football.

Until then, testing of the GT41 continues at several tracks around the world (and, as a reminder, Ford has no aims to run in IMSA or the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2027), while its fresh “Go Like Hell” ad campaign—directed by Zac Snyder and narrated by Matt Damon—will make regular appearances on your various screens for the rest of the year. Including this one, if you click on the video below.

Industry observers note that executive Editor Mike Austin has worked as a writer, editor, and occasional video host across titles such as Car and Driver, Autoblog, Popular Mechanics, and Hemmings (plus a few more). Prior to joining Road & Track he finally put his engineering degrees to use as an EV analyst. His personal cars skew slightly oddball, including a 1991 Honda Beat, 2001 Volkswagen Eurovan, 1987 Alfa Romeo Spider, and 2007 Saab 9-3 wagon.

8 Things You Must Do Before Ending Chapter One in GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1136 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that there is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.
  • Sources indicate that note: It is notable to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that there is a lot that you can do in the first chapter of Grand Theft Auto 6. You can deep sea dive for treasure, hang out with friends, complete missions, set up for Lucia, and a lot more. However, some of this absolutely needs to be done before you hit the end of the first chapter.

After chapter one, everything in GTA 6 changes, and you don’t have the opportunity to get everything done that you might want to, so you want to be sure that you have a checklist and that you complete it before making your way to Vice City and starting bigger and better things.

Sources indicate that note: It is notable to note that taking up Mattia’s offer will end the first chapter of the game. There will also be spoilers ahead about chapter one.

Jason and Lucia have a chance to be madly in love in the beginning of the game. If you prepare for Lucia to get out of prison, work on Jason’s appearance, and focus on how they interact with each other, it will build a solid foundation.

In a recent development, there is a hard reset that comes at the end of the first chapter, and for a while, Lucia will be on her own while Jason recovers. With that being remarked, it will take a bit of a toll on their relationship.

This means that if you raise it up very high in the beginning, you won’t need to worry about needing to rebuild it as much later in the game, saving you a bit of time later on.

Immediately after setting up your BuckMe account, you are told that you need to start saving money. The first goal in the game is to have a total savings of $5,000 stashed away. This is a pretty easy goal to hit, especially since there are a fair number of money-making opportunities in the first chapter.

You want to make sure that you hit this goal, as when the hard reset comes at the end of the chapter, you will lose everything except what is in your savings account.

Recent findings suggest that as an added bonus, putting money away into your savings account will also raise your relationship, so it is a win-win situation. After you have everything saved up, the rest of your money is stuff you can play with.

Now that you have saved up the necessary cash for your family savings account, you might have some money burning a hole in your pocket. It is time to go on a bit of a shopping spree.

Sources indicate that as I mentioned, you won’t be able to take this money with you into chapter two, so you will want to spend all of it. Buy some clothes, and definitely upgrade your weapons.

There is no point in upgrading your car, as you will lose this after chapter one. Instead, focus on increasing your wardrobe and upgrading your weapons as these will carry over into the next chapter.

There are some missions that you only have access to in the first chapter, and some of them belong to Shirley - Jason’s neighbor. She is a kind lady, and she will occasionally ask you to complete a few tasks.

These consist of getting her some alcohol, and stealing a mobility scooter from a lady nearby. They are fun short missions that you can complete within a few minutes, but they are worth doing because they are quite fun.

Don’t worry about the treasure hunting, as you will be able to come back to it later on. Only certain missions disappear after the first chapter.

In a recent development, there’s tons of details in GTA 6, which means that there are a bunch of collectibles that you can find scattered about. Some of these collectibles are books and magazines, and several of them are found around Jason’s house.

Before you end chapter one, you will want to get the books around Jason’s house. These include one in the bedroom, two in the living room, a magazine on the back deck, and one in the shed. Each of these disappears after the first chapter.

In a recent development, along with this, you will want to grab the sunglasses in Donny’s trailer. You will make your way over there during one of the missions in the first chapter, so you shouldn’t miss out on them, but make sure to pick them up while you have the chance.

If you have been focused on upgrading your weapons, gathering clothes, and putting money into your savings, then you will probably need some extra cash in the first chapter. Instead of searching for treasure, you should instead focus on completing the lost drug missions.

There are four lost drug missions around Key Lento and up to the Grassrivers. These are special missions that end up disappearing after chapter one ends, so you will not have the ability to go back and complete them later on.

Since this is the only time you have access to them, you may as well complete them for the extra cash and spend it on stuff that will help you later in the game.

Recent findings suggest that while I have already established that buying weapons is notable because they carry over, it is also important to grab the unique weapons that are obtainable early in the game. There are a couple weapons that you can find around the islands in Key Lento, and they will carry you in later parts of the game.

For instance, the Assassin Pistol can be found on a small dinghy on an island and it is great for completing missions stealthily in later parts of the game, and it has become one of my go-to weapons for staying hidden.

There is also a shotgun that you can find that is quite powerful. It gets outclassed by other unique weapons later on, but it is great to have in chapter two.

According to recent reports, one thing that is nice about GTA 6 is that it gives you the option to manually save. This means that you can create save points at key points in the game so that you can return to them later on.

I highly recommend completing what you can in chapter one and then creating a save point right before you go to do the tourist trap mission, as this is the last mission of the chapter, and it is also the point of no return.

If you want to play the game over but don’t want to deal with the slower pacing of the first chapter, you can skip all of that with a save right before the chapter change.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now released, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

According to recent reports, the recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was confirmed last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy rolled out, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

Industry observers note that the trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

It has been revealed that players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.

Tesla quietly sets up a manufacturer at German machine maker EMAG’s HQ

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1005 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has registered a new German manufacturer whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.
  • But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.
  • Recent findings suggest that the company is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has registered a new German manufacturer whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.

Neither firm confirmed a deal. But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.

Recent findings suggest that the company is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE. Germany’s official company register lists it under HRB 315756 at the Munich district court, with €120,000 in share capital and a business address of Austraße 24 in Salach, a small town east of Stuttgart. That’s EMAG’s home base.

It didn’t start out as a Tesla firm. The register shows it was first entered on August 26 as “Blitz 26-299 SE,” a shell company. Law firms sell these pre-registered shells so buyers can skip weeks of incorporation paperwork, and Tesla renamed this one earlier this month.

Business Insider Germany, which reported the change based on a notice in the federal gazette, notes three people run it: Maximilian Stromberger, Tesla Germany’s 33-year-old head of sales, an American robotics engineer, and the head of HR at Tesla’s Grünheide factory.

In a recent development, the HR chief is the interesting name. You don’t need one to hold a passive stake in a supplier, but you do if you’re about to take on employees.

Neither Tesla nor EMAG answered Business Insider’s repeated requests for comment.

According to recent reports, local press near Salach has been on this for over a week. On November 23, the Stuttgarter Nachrichten reported that signs of a Tesla entry were piling up and that EMAG had briefed its workforce at a large staff meeting the week before. Business Insider dates that meeting to November 16.

Today, the same paper went further. It reports that around 220 EMAG employees will move to Tesla, that the two companies have been working together for some time, and that the deal is about humanoid robots. The full story is paywalled, and none of it has been confirmed by either manufacturer.

EMAG, with roots going back to 1867, makes turning, grinding, and gear-cutting machines, mostly for car parts like transmissions and drivetrains. The auto slowdown hit it hard. A year ago, EMAG remarked it would cut 455 jobs in Germany, roughly 300 of them in Salach, which is about a third of its domestic staff. It lost €42 million on €496 million of revenue in 2024, per Business Insider. It has been talking to potential investors ever since.

In a recent development, but EMAG has also been chasing a upcoming market. Its website has an entire section on manufacturing humanoid robot actuator parts: flexsplines, wave generators, and planetary gears.

Industry observers note that the first two make up a strain wave gear, the compact, high-reduction gearbox used in robot joints. Planetary gears go in the bigger joints that carry more load. EMAG says its machines hold these parts to ISO 1328 Class 4 gear quality, with runout under 5 micrometers, and can repeat that in high-volume production.

In a recent development, that’s right where Tesla states it’s stuck. On the Q3 earnings call last month, Musk called the hand Optimus’ main hardware problem and flagged custom gears as a reliability worry, as we reported at the time. Tesla is installing a Fremont line designed for a million robots a year, and the Optimus design it showed in 2022 used 28 structural actuators per robot. At that volume, you’re talking about tens of millions of actuators a year, many of them built around precision gears that few suppliers can make consistently.

Recent findings suggest that tesla moving directly into precision tooling highlights a brutal reality for robotics founders: software gets the spotlight, but high-tolerance actuator supply chains dictate your unit economics and scale. Building physical AI means mastering industrial manufacturing long before mass production begins. When navigating high-stakes hardware trade-offs and specialized talent, having early backers who have built hardware companies matters. Grove Ventures works hands-on from pre-seed with deeptech and AI founders, offering real operator experience to help scale complex physical architectures.

Sources indicate that tesla is already building the German side of this. In July, Tesla started recruiting in Reutlingen to develop and manufacture Optimus parts, including sensors, gearboxes, and actuators, plus the equipment to mass-produce them. Reutlingen is the former Manz site that Tesla took over in early 2025, along with about 300 of its employees.

According to recent reports, tesla has done this before. It agreed to buy Grohmann Engineering in Prüm in late 2016, which became Tesla Automation, and that unit absorbed the Manz operations. Tesla is also putting €3 billion into a Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin.

Tesla briefly acquired Wiferion in Germany. Tesla did buy the wireless charging startup in 2023, but it sold the business a few months later and kept the engineers.

  • Recent findings suggest that suzuki left the U.S.

  • It has been revealed that A 26-kilowatt-hour lithium iron phosphate battery sits under the floor of Suzuki’s dedicated Heartect-e electric platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that suzuki left the U.S. car market in 2012, but it still builds the kind of small hatchbacks European buyers have long favored, now also powered by electricity. Its latest is the Ignis EV, a city car that measures just 11 feet 9 inches long (3.57 meters). It’s due in Europe in summer 2027, when it will face a newly introduced generation of small EVs from both European and Chinese automakers.

The Ignis is Suzuki’s first subcompact electric car developed for global markets, but its roots are in Japan. The tech giant recently introduced the e Sky there, an electric kei car that supplies the basis for the Ignis’s body and powertrain. The Ignis still has the typical kei proportions (it's tall and narrow), but Suzuki notes it took the car onto European city streets and winding roads to tune the suspension and power delivery, making it more appealing to the people it hopes will buy one.

It has been revealed that A 26-kilowatt-hour lithium iron phosphate battery sits under the floor of Suzuki’s dedicated Heartect-e electric platform. Yes, that really is what it's called. Up front, the motor, inverter, and reduction gears share a single compact assembly that sends 90 horsepower and 98 pound-feet (133 Nm) to the front wheels. Suzuki says it chose LFP for safety and longevity, but it hasn’t given the European car a range or charging figure yet.

The Ignis EV has a very tight 29.5-foot (9-meter) turning circle. Its overhangs are tiny, giving it a wheel-at-each-corner stance that looks unique while maximizing available interior room. The LED signatures at both ends take their shape from digital numerals, and the dark pillars give the roof a floating look.

According to recent reports, inside, a curve runs from the dashboard into the doors, with a wide display and a ceramic-inspired storage tray across the dash. Suzuki President Toshihiro Suzuki credits the organization’s decades of building Japanese mini vehicles for its ability to provide a genuinely usable cabin in such a small footprint.

Recent findings suggest that for decades, European brands had most of this business to themselves. If you wanted an inexpensive car that could squeeze down a narrow street, Fiat would happily sell you a Panda, Renault a Twingo and Volkswagen an Up. Chinese automakers see an opening as those buyers go electric.

In a recent development, leapmotor brought the T03 to Europe through its partnership with Stellantis, while BYD adapted its Chinese-market Seagull for Europe and called it the Dolphin Surf. Driving the latter, what stood out to me was how well it drove, how little felt cheap, and how much kit it had for its sub-€20,000 starting price.

Sources indicate that by the time the Ignis arrives next year, European buyers will have had plenty of practice shopping for small EVs. Renault has revived both the 5 and the Twingo as electric cars, and there’s also the related Dacia Spring. Volkswagen has the ID. Polo, Cupra has the Raval, and Skoda has the Epiq, and there definitely seems to be demand for them. In September, a major VW dealer group reported more than 30,000 orders for the ID. Polo and a waiting list stretching to ten months.

That leaves one big question for the little Suzuki. What will it cost? Consider the redesigned Dacia Spring. Dacia moved production from China to Slovenia, shared the electric Twingo’s underpinnings, and produced a car that starts at €17,900 in Italy. It gets up to 155 miles (250 kilometers) of WLTP range from a battery only slightly larger than the one in the Ignis.

Breaking: The Tesla Cybertruck Is America’s Fastest-Selling Used Truck

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even though it was recently canceled, the Tesla Cybertruck is the number-one-selling used car in America.
  • In fact, EVs take 25 percent less time to sell than gas vehicles in the used market, and among those EVs there are three Teslas in the top 25, including the Cybertruck, Model 3, and Model Y.
  • “Why do so many electric vehicles, including the recently canceled Cybertruck, sell so rapidly on the used market?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though it was recently canceled, the Tesla Cybertruck is the number-one-selling used car in America. That’s based on analysis of over 1.1 million used-vehicle sales from October 2026 by iSeeCars.com. It includes the fastest-selling trucks and the 25 fastest- and slowest-selling vehicles overall.

In fact, EVs take 25 percent less time to sell than gas vehicles in the used market, and among those EVs there are three Teslas in the top 25, including the Cybertruck, Model 3, and Model Y. And 16 of the 25 fastest-selling used vehicles are EVs.

“Why do so many electric vehicles, including the recently canceled Cybertruck, sell so rapidly on the used market? The combination of sustained high fuel prices and a dramatic drop in market value essentially ‘flips the script’ on EVs when they transition from new to used status,” noted iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer.

Industry observers note that here are some numbers: EVs average 45.6 days on the market compared with 54.5 days for hybrids and 61.0 days for gasoline vehicles, according to iSeeCars. Those 45.6 days are 15.4 days less than gasoline vehicles and 8.9 days less than hybrids. The overall industry average is 59.5 days. Used EVs spend 25.2 percent less time on the market than gasoline vehicles, while hybrids spend 10.7 percent less time on the market than gasoline models.

See all results for new 2026 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 72058.

In a recent development, and despite the fact that many electric pickup trucks have recently been axed, EV pickups in general are particularly well represented among the fastest-selling used trucks, the study claims. Four of the top 10 trucks are electric, and three of them rank among the top four fastest-selling pickups.

The Tesla Cybertruck leads the rankings at 39.1 days on the market, selling in 26.4 fewer days than the average used pickup. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second at 43.3 days, followed by the fully electric Rivian R1T at 45.2 days and the Ford F-150 Lightning at 47.4 days.

Gasoline-powered trucks account for five of the top 10 positions, led by the Toyota Tacoma in fifth place at 50.1 days. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second, outperforming all electric trucks except the Cybertruck.

However, not every electric pickup sells quickly. The Chevrolet Silverado EV ranks last among all 24 trucks, averaging 107.5 days on the market. That’s 68.4 days longer than the Cybertruck and 42.0 days longer than the average truck.

EVs also perform strongly in the broader used market, per iSeeCars, where they claim 16 of the 25 fastest-selling model rankings.

The Audi A4 Allroad is the fastest-selling used vehicle overall, averaging just over a month on the market, or 33.7 days, followed by the Lexus RX 450h+ plug-in hybrid at 35.0 days and Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron at 36.3 days.

See all results for new 2026 Tesla Cybertruck for sale near 72058.

It has been revealed that electric vehicles occupy six of the top 10 positions, including the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron, Audi Q6 e-tron, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Lexus RZ 300e, Kia EV9, and BMW i5. All six average fewer than 39 days on the market, compared with the overall used vehicle average of 59.5 days.

It has been revealed that the Tesla Cybertruck ranks 16th among all used vehicles, averaging 39.1 days, while the Tesla Model 3 ranks 18th at 39.5 days and Tesla Model Y ranks 24th at 39.8 days. Electric models from Kia, Rivian, Subaru, Toyota, and Volkswagen also appear in the top 25.

What are the slowest sellers on the used car market? The Cadillac Escalade IQ is the slowest-selling vehicle in the study, averaging 134.3 days on the market, more than twice the overall industry average. The Ford Escape plug-in hybrid ranks second at 127.3 days, followed by the Lincoln Corsair hybrid at 114.0 days.

The Silverado EV ranks fourth at 107.5 days, making it both the slowest-selling electric pickup and one of the slowest-selling used vehicles overall.

Two additional electric vehicles appear among the slowest-selling models: the electric Dodge Charger, averaging 98.2 days, and the GMC Hummer EV SUV, averaging 84.9 days.

According to recent reports, “There’s clearly a big shift from fresh to used status for electric vehicles, especially when fuel prices have remained elevated for several months,” said Brauer. “Used shoppers are all about value, which normally plays against electric vehicles. But when consumers see their fuel budget jump 20 to 30 percent, the value of not visiting a gas station leads straight to used EVs.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it's been less than a week since Grand Theft Auto 6 came out, and Rockstar Games has already found another way to get us to spend money on the game. If you've been collecting sports cards while exploring Leonida, you'll soon be able to do the same outside the game. Rockstar has partnered with Panini America to bring these fictional sports trading cards to life, and they'll be out in December 2026.

It has been revealed that this goes beyond your usual video game merchandise featuring the main characters. The cards are based on collectibles that actually exist within GTA 6's world, so you might recognize some of the athletes and teams when you open a pack. And if you're hoping to get your hands on some of the rarer cards, there are even a few that are limited to a single copy each.

Recent findings suggest that panini America unveiled its partnership with Rockstar Games on November 24. The officially licensed set is called the GTA VI: Sports Trading Card Collection, and it'll be the first trading card collaboration between the two companies.

Industry observers note that if you've ever collected football or basketball cards, chances are you're already familiar with Panini. They're also known for reprinting comics in Europe, and I still have a copy of the X-Men: The Last Stand Annual 2007 published by Panini Books.

It has been revealed that what's different this time is that instead of collecting cards featuring actual sports stars, you'll be collecting ones based on athletes from Rockstar's fictional universe. The promotional artwork demonstrates a mixture of illustrated cards and ones featuring character renders, much like those found in the game itself.

Industry observers note that the cards will come in boxes containing four packs each. Panini says a box will typically include two Rookie cards, a Retro card, an Illustrated card and four Special Silvers. These are average figures rather than guaranteed contents for every box.

Industry observers note that there'll also be different colored variants of the cards, including silver, pink, teal and light blue, along with team-colored parallels. The rarest variants have much smaller print runs. The Legend Bronze cards are numbered out of 49, the numbered Silver variants out of 25, and the Gold variants are one-of-a-kind cards.

Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn’t be surprised if some of the rare cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

Sources indicate that getting your hands on every variant, however, could be quite a challenge. Considering how many people are playing GTA 6 right now, I wouldn't be surprised if some of the rarer cards ended up selling for ridiculous prices.

Even if you don't care about the numbered cards, there's some appeal in having the regular ones. GTA's fictional athletes aren't exactly household names like the ones you'd find in Panini's other sports collections, but you can actually go looking for their cards in Leonida while playing the game.

Industry observers note that rockstar has been selling GTA merchandise for years, but this particular collaboration reminds me of the sort of extras that used to come with physical copies of video games. The maps that came with older GTA titles, for instance, were something you could actually use while playing and keep long after you were done with the game.

According to recent reports, ironically, GTA 6's boxed edition doesn't even come with a game disc. So it's nice to see Rockstar making something physical that draws directly from the game rather than simply putting its logo on another piece of merchandise.

Rockstar could've easily gone with a conventional trading card set featuring Jason, Lucia, and other major characters. Instead, it's making replicas of things you might stumble across while taking a break from the story. I'd love to see Rockstar do something similar with other fictional brands from the series, like Sprunk or eCola.

Unfortunately, Panini hasn't unveiled an exact release date, pricing, or which countries the cards will be available in.

Depending on when the cards go on sale in December, they could make for a pretty good Christmas gift for a GTA fan.

In a recent development, ionna, the EV charging network that ranked first in J.D. Power’s latest public charging satisfaction survey, has slashed prices at its stations across the country for Thanksgiving weekend.

According to recent reports, the firm, which usually charges an average of $0.40/kilowatt-hour, is now asking for $0.20/kWh plus tax at all its DC fast charging stations in the United States. That’s a 50% discount, and drivers don’t have to do anything special to get it—just plug in and pay, either through the automaker’s official smartphone app, the on-site payment terminals, or the Presto app for Tesla owners who want to enjoy the Autocharge function.

Recent findings suggest that for long-distance travel, the slashed charging rates can make a substantial difference. A single 50-kilowatt-hour session that used to cost $20 will now be just $10 plus tax, but seeing how many people are traveling across the country these days, multiple sessions will be necessary, driving the cost savings even further.

Sources indicate that and it’s not like the cost reduction comes with any strings attached. Ionna uses 400-kilowatt chargers from Alpitronic exclusively, so there’s plenty of wiggle room for even the most power-hungry EVs out there. What’s more, many stalls have dual cords for each port, with a CCS2 connector and a NACS connector, so charging adapters aren’t needed at most locations.

Separately, Ionna has discounts for several automakers, including Mercedes-Benz, BMW, General Motors, and Stellantis.

Sources indicate that the charging operator installed its first stalls in 2024, and it has wasted no time expanding its footprint swiftly. On its second anniversary, Ionna celebrated by opening its 100th site, and the manufacturer now has 229 sites and nearly 1,900 ports nationwide, according to the Department of Energy's Alternative Fuels Data Center (AFDC). Still, the charging network is not slowing down, with dozens of locations under construction and plans to introduce 500-kW chargers in the near future.

According to recent reports, most EV brands support Plug & Charge at Ionna, with Tesla recently getting Autocharge functionality through a third-party smartphone application. Ionna itself doesn’t have a smartphone app, instead relying on automakers and third-party apps to integrate its locations. So far, this approach has turned out to be quite successful, with J.D. Power’s latest public charging survey putting the operator first, ahead of Tesla and the rest of the competition.

Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating.
  • It has been revealed that the results were especially striking for people with prediabetes.
  • In a recent development, "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," claims Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A ketogenic diet may offer significant health benefits beyond weight loss, according to a new clinical trial that compared three popular approaches to eating. Researchers found that people following a very low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet experienced substantially greater reductions in liver fat than those eating Mediterranean or low-fat diets, even though all three groups lost similar amounts of weight.

It has been revealed that the results were especially striking for people with prediabetes. After just four to five months on a ketogenic (or "Keto") diet, approximately half of the participants no longer met the diagnostic criteria for the condition. The findings, published in the journal Cell Metabolism, suggest that the types of foods people eat can influence metabolic health in ways that extend beyond the number of pounds they lose.

In a recent development, "We know weight loss can improve metabolic health in people who are obese," claims Samuel Klein, the study's corresponding author at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis, Missouri. "Our data suggest that if you have high liver fat content and prediabetes, reducing carbohydrate intake can have vital therapeutic effects on metabolism beyond just weight loss alone.".

Comparing Keto, Mediterranean, and Low-Fat Diets.

Sources indicate that an estimated 40% of American adults have obesity, a condition associated with increased risks of type 2 diabetes, fatty liver disease, and other health problems. Doctors frequently recommend dietary changes to help patients lose weight and improve their metabolic health, which refers to how effectively the body manages energy, blood sugar, and fats.

Three commonly recommended approaches are low-carbohydrate diets, low-fat diets, and Mediterranean diets. Although each can support weight loss, researchers have been uncertain whether one offers additional metabolic advantages when the amount of weight lost is roughly the same.

According to recent reports, these eating patterns differ substantially in their nutritional makeup. Low-carbohydrate approaches, including Atkins and ketogenic diets, restrict carbohydrate consumption, while low-fat diets may obtain as much as 70% of their calories from carbohydrates. The Mediterranean diet emphasizes plant foods such as vegetables, nuts, and olive oil, along with moderate amounts of fish and dairy. Ketogenic diets, meanwhile, can include considerable amounts of fat from animal products, including saturated fat.

Industry observers note that to compare their effects, Klein and his colleagues recruited 42 adults with obesity, prediabetes, and fatty liver disease. Prediabetes occurs when blood sugar levels rise above the normal range but have not yet reached the threshold for type 2 diabetes. Fatty liver disease involves excess fat accumulating inside liver cells, which can interfere with the body's ability to regulate metabolism.

A Controlled Clinical Trial With Similar Weight Loss.

Industry observers note that participants were randomly assigned to follow one of three diets: ketogenic, Mediterranean, or a low-fat diet emphasizing plant-based foods. To ensure that participants followed their assigned eating looks, the research team supplied all their meals and arranged weekly consultations with a dietitian.

The diets had sharply different proportions of carbohydrates and fat. In the ketogenic group, carbohydrates accounted for just 4% of daily calories, while fat supplied 73%. The Mediterranean group received 50% of its calories from carbohydrates and 35% from fat. The plant-forward group consumed 70% of its calories from carbohydrates and 15% from fat.

Researchers adjusted calorie intake individually so that participants across all three groups lost approximately 10% of their starting body weight. Reaching this target took about four to five months.

According to recent reports, by the end of the intervention, every group had experienced meaningful reductions in body fat and improvements in insulin sensitivity. Insulin is the hormone that helps move sugar from the bloodstream into cells, where it can be used for energy. Greater insulin sensitivity makes it easier for the body to maintain healthy blood sugar levels.

However, the similarities between the groups largely ended there.

Keto Diet Reduces Liver Fat by 67%.

The ketogenic diet produced the largest improvements in several important indicators of liver function and metabolic health.

Industry observers note that participants following keto experienced an average 67% reduction in liver fat, compared with a 45% reduction in both the Mediterranean and low-fat groups. Because the groups lost comparable amounts of weight, the difference suggests that carbohydrate restriction may influence liver fat through mechanisms beyond weight loss alone.

To investigate these effects, the researchers collected blood samples repeatedly over a 24-hour period, allowing them to observe changes in hormones involved in energy metabolism.

Industry observers note that the ketogenic group showed the greatest increase in glucagon, a hormone that helps regulate the body's energy supply and promotes the reduction of fat stored in the liver. Participants on keto also experienced the largest decrease in insulin levels, another change that can help reduce liver fat accumulation.

It has been revealed that one result was particularly unexpected. Despite getting nearly three-quarters of their calories from fat, the keto participants did not show an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels during the study.

"The most surprising finding was that participants in the ketogenic diet group didn't experience an increase in blood fat or cholesterol levels despite consuming the most fat," says Max Petersen, the study's first author at Washington University School of Medicine.

Half of Keto Participants No Longer Had Prediabetes.

In a recent development, the benefits extended beyond liver fat. After the weight-loss intervention, approximately 50% of participants assigned to the ketogenic diet no longer met the criteria for prediabetes. By comparison, that milestone was reached by 29% of those on the Mediterranean diet and just 7% of those following the low-fat, plant-forward diet.

According to recent reports, these differences are notable because prediabetes signals an elevated risk of developing type 2 diabetes. Bringing blood sugar levels below the prediabetes threshold is an key improvement, although it does not necessarily mean the condition has been permanently reversed.

Recent findings suggest that the findings also highlight a potentially vital distinction in weight management: losing weight and improving metabolic health are closely connected, but they are not necessarily the same thing. The composition of a diet may affect how the body handles blood sugar, stores fat, and responds to hormones, even when weight loss is similar.

In a recent development, researchers emphasize the growing importance of understanding these effects as powerful latest obesity treatments become more widely available. GLP-1 medications, which act on hormone pathways involved in appetite and blood sugar regulation, have transformed the treatment of obesity by helping many patients achieve substantial weight loss.

"GLP-1-based medications have revolutionized the therapy of obesity. We now have a very effective pharmacotherapy for achieving significant weight loss," Petersen says. "But in addition, our study shows that the specific composition of the diet can give you added benefits.".

Industry observers note that although the trial was relatively small and lasted only four to five months, its carefully controlled design offers evidence that dietary composition can play an important role in metabolic health. Longer studies involving more participants will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist and how different diets compare over time.

The research was supported by the National Institutes of Health and the Foundation for Barnes-Jewish Hospital.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh Arc Raiders patch has arrived, bringing a host of newly introduced fixes to several exploits players have recently been relying on to do things they’re not supposed to, and bypass certain mechanics to get into areas without having to go through proper channels.

The patch is fairly small, and surprisingly doesn’t include any buffs or nerfs to anything in particular.

The list of notes for update 1.4.0 is compact, with a clear focus on addressing several exploits. The biggest one, of course, is the addition of “exploit mitigation mechanisms” to stop players from glitching through locked doors.

This fix applies to all maps, and it’s intended to address an glitch whereby players would not bring the required keys to access those areas of the various maps. Locked rooms, if they can be unlocked, often hide a wealth of high-tier and rare loot.

But players have also been using similar exploits to clip through walls and access areas outside the playspace, allowing them to ambush enemy players and set up traps that would be impossible for others to detect.

According to recent reports, the game’s recent patch, which was released exactly one week ago, mainly consisted of balance tweaks to some of the more popular weapons and mines. However, it also introduced a few fixes to prevent players from clipping through walls by using barricades.

While on the subject of being in places where you’re not supposed to, the patch blocked exterior access to the locked room inside Spaceport's Control Tower, making it only accessible from inside the tower.

In a recent development, 1.4.0 also fixes an especially nasty exploit that allowed players to bring up their weapons much faster than normal by promptly swapping to the quick use menu. There’s a range of smaller fixes for lighting and texture bugs here, too, and you can read all about it in the full change log below:.
